subject: Literature
title: Philip K. Dick's Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
description: A 60-second lesson on Philip K. Dick's Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?.

hook.text: Philip K. Dick asked whether a robot who believes it is human deserves the same empathy as a biological person.

buildup.text: In a post-nuclear Earth, bounty hunter Rick Deckard 'retires' androids who are almost indistinguishable from humans.

discovery.text: The empathy test used to detect androids reveals that some humans score lower than the machines they are hunting.

twist.text: Dick was paranoid, impoverished, and possibly mentally ill, yet his novels now define how we think about artificial minds.

climax.text: The novel asks the question that haunts our AI age: what makes someone human when machines can think and feel?

punchline.text: He asked what makes us human before we had to answer.

quiz.question: What disturbing discovery does the empathy test reveal?
options: All androids have perfect empathy scores
Some humans score lower on empathy than the androids being hunted
The test cannot detect any difference between humans and androids
